_about: Researched claims with their evidence (research track R, ROADMAP.md). Each source gives what it is (kind: primary = a document of the time or a record made from the fabric; listing = an official heritage register description; secondary = a history or report; reference = an encyclopaedia or aggregator), where in it (locator) and an exact short quote that `python -m bidb.evidence --check` looks for in the source again. verdict: kept (the catalogue's value stands), corrected (see date_corrections.json), open. Compiled with AI assistance; quotes are checked automatically, judgements are not.

claims.name: Althorp
claims.claim: The house was begun c. 1508 for John Spencer and remodelled in the 1660s and by Henry Holland in 1786–91; Wikipedia's 'dates to 1688' is not the date of the house.
claims.assessment: The statutory list description dates the house to c. 1508 for John Spencer, who bought the estate that year. Wikipedia's lead sentence ('dates to 1688') is uncited there and rests in the body on one early-19th-century account (Jones 1829, p. 245); the same article dates the staircase to the 1660s, so the house existed before 1688. 1688 is best read as a phase of the late-17th-century rebuilding, not the origin of the house.

claims.claim: Jews' Court dates from c. 1170 (altered in the early 17th century); a charter of 1316 puts the medieval synagogue in the tenement behind it, so the building itself was probably not the synagogue.
claims.assessment: The date stands. The synagogue identification (Cecil Roth) is weakened by the documents the source cites (1290 division into two houses; 1316 charter placing the scola to the west, behind). The research file already calls it 'claimed'; the type 'oldest synagogue' should not rest on it.
